entities.summary: Jean de Bertrand was a Roman Catholic cardinal. He was born in unknown dates and died on December 14, 1560. Jean de Bertrand was a key figure in the Catholic Church during the Renaissance. He played a significant role in the papal conclave of 1559, which led to the election of Pope Pius IV. Jean de Bertrand's influence extended to the Italian city-states, where he collaborated with the Medici family. He was a member of the College of Cardinals and participated in several important councils. Jean de Bertrand's legacy includes his contributions to the Catholic Church's reform efforts and his role in shaping the papacy's relations with European monarchs. He was also a notable figure in the history of the Sistine Chapel, where he oversaw several artistic projects. Jean de Bertrand's life and career demonstrate the complex web of relationships between the Catholic Church, European politics, and artistic patronage during the Renaissance. Despite his significant impact, Jean de Bertrand's life remains somewhat overshadowed by the more prominent figures of the era.
